comment_corrections: Original bounded persistent dump and transfer schedule.
Port retention limits, GUI window and transfer schedule.
* Unlike GT6's static lists this survives restarts as world SavedData.

* GT6 also saves its static pools through GarbageGT server save/load hooks.
 * This port stores the server-wide pools in overworld SavedData.

*

A pile merges by {@link ItemStack#isSameItemSameTags}, so a stack carrying per-instance NBT * (a used tool, a charged battery, a bee's random genome) never merges with anything: every trashed * stack became a new permanent entry. Nothing else removes an entry - the only removal * path is {@link #extractItem} draining that exact pile to zero - so the list grew with every * NBT-carrying stack the Ender Garbage Bin ever voided, in the heap and in the world save alike. * Past this cap the oldest pile is dropped, which bounds the dump while leaving the behaviour for * every dump a player can actually reach through the container (it shows 54 piles) unchanged.

*

Equal item/tag or component combinations merge; distinct combinations use separate entries. * Adding a new entry at this cap discards the oldest pile, including one visible in the first * 54 GUI slots. This is the port's bounded retention policy, rather than an original GT6 limit. * The original pool also persists, but does not impose this entry cap.
One merged garbage pile: an item template (count 1) plus an unbounded count.
One merged garbage pile: an item template (count 1) plus a long count.
ItemStack.save clamps Count to a byte, so the real count is kept beside it
Keep the pool count separately; the saved item template represents one item

readability.scope: Full ordered code and literal positions after recorded local-name normalization, including inactive Stonecutter code; other comments/directives retained. No algorithm or data/schema changes.

formal_findings_added.finding: Bin uses only world-time modulo; original entity-local cadence also flushes on block update.
Powered bin rejects automatic item insertion; original only pauses trashing while insertion remains permitted.
Automatic dump only offers first item/fluid, so an unsuitable head blocks a later acceptable candidate.
Dump output cadence/budget changed: every server tick and unrestricted fluid iteration to every ten ticks, one item and 16000 L first fluid.
Dump passive item/fluid and tap/nozzle exports are not bound; GUI extraction/own downward tick do not replace them.

Each item/fluid pool is independently capped at 256 identities with earliest eviction; item GUI view is fixed at 54. Original has no identity cap. Existing oversized load keeps earliest instead; preserve protective policy pending explicit redesign.
Amount domains changed: original item counters int-saturate and fluid pools use long capacity; current item count is long and fluids int-saturate.
Source-reachable empty-hotbar SWAP copies the displayed pool stack without decreasing real stock because the view setter is no-op. High priority; no native world reproduction.
Bin removal actively scatters local buffer, while original canDrop=false and keepSlot=false do not return it this way.
Original internal admin-dump blacklist is absent from current global intake.
Original dump can eject items into collision-free air below through ST.put; current lower-null check stops before any attempt.

formal_findings_extended.scope: Original bin all-side cover prohibition is not retained by generic fallback admission. Dump does not override this old prohibition, so do not extend to dump.

source_witnesses.conditions: Pool holds stone then iron; lower valid inventory rejects stone and accepts iron, with room for 64. Old scans beyond first candidate; current only offers pool index zero. Fluid variant: first fluid rejected, second accepted; old iterable continues, current only offers first.

Server dump menu, pool slot zero has 64 ordinary stackable items; target hotbar slot empty. viewItem returns a 64-item copy, mayPickup simulates successfully, vanilla SWAP puts it into hotbar and calls slot setter with empty; no-op view setter and ordinary onTake leave pool at 64.
source_witnesses.limit: Ordered source/actual native consumer inference, not executed menu/game/network test.

source_witnesses.conditions: Adding a 257th distinct identity removes entry zero, including a first-page entry. No original trim. Existing oversized port data load stops after earliest 256; source policy difference, no actual saved-world test.

One more litre after Integer.MAX_VALUE: old long-capacity pool can hold 2147483648, current fluidMerge retains 2147483647. Conversely current item long can retain more than original int-saturated count; no overflow gameplay exploit claimed.
Below at ordinary y=64 is air and has no block entity; original ST.move enables ejection and ST.put passes collision-free branch, current returns at below==null. No dropped entity execution.

already_implemented_or_rejected: Original GarbageGT static lists already save/load both pools, and GT_API_Proxy calls those methods. Persistence is not a newly added feature, contrary to the old source comment.
Current dimensions share server.overworld SavedData; no per-dimension partition finding. Real disk save/restart not tested.
Identical item tags/components can merge; per-instance NBT does not automatically make every stack unmergeable. Comment corrected.
Bin fluid input is immediate into pool and pauses with redstone in both sources; item insertion difference is not generalized to fluid acceptance.
Dump refusal to return output directly into a bin exists in both implementations.
Current shift-click menu explicitly extracts and re-trashes remainder; do not call every menu path duplicating. SWAP uses a distinct inherited path.
Bounded retention, int/long choices and new GUI are policy differences, not instructions to remove protection or restore unsafe growth.
